questions.question: A transverse wave travels on a taut steel wire with a velocity of $v$ when tension in it is $2.06 \times {10}^{4}N.$ When the tension is changed to $T,$ the velocity changed to $\frac{v}{2}.$ The value of $T$ is close to:
questions.explanation: $v \propto \sqrt{T} \implies \frac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}}} \implies \frac{v}{\left(\frac{v}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{\frac{2.06 \times {10}^{4}}{T}} \implies T = \frac{2.06 \times {10}^{4}}{4}N = 0.515 \times {10}^{4}N$

questions.question: A $25m$ long antenna is mounted on an antenna tower. The height of the antenna tower is $75m$. The wavelength (in meter) of the signal transmitted by this antenna would be :
questions.explanation:
Length of Antena $= 25m = \frac{\lambda }{4} \implies \lambda = 100m$

.

questions.question: A transverse harmonic wave on a string is given by $y\left(x,t\right) = 5\sin \left(6t + 0.003x\right)$ where $x$ and $y$ are in $\mathrm{cm}$ and $t$ in $\sec$. The wave velocity is _________ $m{s}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation:
The general equation for a wave can be written as $y = A\sin \left(\omega t + kx\right)$. Comparing it with the given equation, $y = 5\sin \left(6t + 0.003x\right)$,

$\omega = 6\mathrm{rad}{s}^{ - 1}$, $k = 0.003{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 1}$

Using the equation, $v = \frac{\omega }{k} v = \frac{6}{0.003 \times {10}^{2}} = 20m{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: A heavy ball of mass $M$ is suspended from the ceiling of a car by a light string of mass $m\left(m≪M\right).$ When the car is at rest, the speed of transverse waves in the string is $60{\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 1}.$ When the car has acceleration $a,$ the wave-speed increases to $60.5{\mathrm{ms}}^{ - 1}.$ The value of $a,$ in terms of gravitational acceleration $g,$ is closed to
questions.explanation: For standing car, $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }} = \sqrt{\frac{Mg}{\mu }}$ For accelerating car, $\upsilon ′ = \sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{{(Mg)}^{2} + {(Ma)}^{2}}}{\mu }} \implies \frac{60.5}{60} = \sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{{(Mg)}^{2} + {(Ma)}^{2}}}{Mg}} \implies {\left(1 + \frac{1}{120}\right)}^{2} = \frac{\sqrt{{(Mg)}^{2} + {(Ma)}^{2}}}{Mg} \implies 1 + \frac{2}{120} = \sqrt{1 + \frac{{a}^{2}}{{g}^{2}}} \approx \frac{2}{120} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{{a}^{2}}{{g}^{2}} ∴a = g\sqrt{\frac{4}{120}} = \frac{g}{\sqrt{30}} \approx \frac{g}{5}$

questions.question: A longitudinal wave is represented by $y = 10\sin 2\pi \left(nt - \frac{x}{\lambda }\right)\mathrm{cm}$. The maximum particle velocity will be four times the wave velocity if the determined value of wavelength is equal to
questions.explanation:
As we know particle velocity, {v}_{p} = \frac{dy}{dt} = \left(10 \times 2\pi n\right) \times \cos 2\pi \left(nt - \frac{x}{\lambda }\right)$

Therefore, {\left({v}_{p}\right)}_{max} = 20\pi n$

Now as we know, $v = \lambda n$

As given in the question,

{\left({v}_{p}\right)}_{max} = 4v\;$

questions.question: Assume that the displacement (s) of air is proportional to the pressure difference $\left(\Delta p\right)$ created by a sound wave. Displacement (s) further depends on the speed of sound (v), density of air$\left(\rho \right)$ and the frequency (f). If $\Delta p~10Pa,n~300m / s,p~1kg / {m}^{3} f~1000Hz$, then s will be of the order of (take the multiplicative constant to be 1 )
questions.explanation:
$S = \frac{{P}_{0}}{BK} = \frac{{P}_{0}}{P{V}^{2}\frac{\omega }{V}} = \frac{{P}_{0}}{P{V}_{\omega }} = \frac{10}{1 \times 1000 \times 300}m ≃\frac{3}{100}\mathrm{mm}$

`

questions.question: The mass per unit length of a uniform wire is $0.135g{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 1}$. A transverse wave of the form $y = - 0.21\sin \left(x + 30t\right)$ is produced in it, where $x$ is in meter and $t$ is in second. Then, the expected value of tension in the wire is $x \times {10}^{ - 2}N$. Value of $x$ is <u> </u> (Round-off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
$\mu = 0.135\mathrm{gm}{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 1} = 0.0135\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 1} y = - 0.21\sin \left(x + 30t\right)$

($x$ in meter & $t$ in sec)

$v = \frac{\omega }{k} = \frac{30}{1} = 30m{s}^{ - 1} v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }} \implies T = {v}^{2}\mu = {\left(30\right)}^{2}\left(0.0135\right) = 12.15 = x \times {10}^{ - 2}N \implies x = 1215$

questions.question: The equation of wave is given by $Y = {10}^{ - 2}\sin 2\pi \left(160t - 0.5x + \frac{\pi }{4}\right)$, where $x$ and $Y$ are in $m$ and $t$ in $s$. The speed of the wave is _______ $\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation:
The equation of the wave is

$Y = {10}^{ - 2}\sin 2\pi (160t - 0.5x + \frac{\pi }{4})$

The velocity of a wave is given by $v = \frac{\omega }{k}...(i)$.

A wave equation is given by

$Y = A\sin \left(\omega t - kx + ϕ\right)$

Using equation (i),

$v = \left(\frac{2\pi \times 160}{2\pi \times 0.5}\right) = 320m{{s}^{ - 1}}_{} \implies v = 320 \times \frac{18}{5} \implies v = 1152\mathrm{km}{h}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: The distance between two consecutive points with phase difference of $60 ^\circ$ in a wave of frequency $500\mathrm{Hz}$ is $6.0m$. The velocity with which wave is travelling is ______ $\mathrm{km}{s}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation:
Distance between two consecutive points $60 ^\circ$ out of phase is given by $\Delta x = \frac{\lambda }{2\pi }\Delta ϕ$

Putting the values, we have

$6 = \frac{\lambda }{2\pi }\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right) \implies \lambda = 36m$

Now, velocity of wave is $v = f\lambda = (500\mathrm{Hz})(36m) = 18000m{s}^{ - 1} = 18\mathrm{km}{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: Displacement of a wave is expressed as $x(t)=5 \cos \left(628 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) m$. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is $300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=5 \cos \left[628 \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{2}\right] \mathrm{m} \\ & \text { velocity }\left(\mathrm{v}_\omega\right)=300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{K}} \\ & 300=\frac{628}{\mathrm{~K}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}=\frac{628}{300} \\ & \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}=\frac{628}{300} \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{2 \times 3.14 \times 300}{628} \\ & \lambda=2 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A plane progressive wave is given by $y=2 \cos 2 \pi(330 \mathrm{t}-x) \mathrm{m}$. The frequency of the wave is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & y=2 \cos 2 \pi(330 t-x) m \\ & y=A \cos (\omega t-k x) \\ & \text { by comparing } \omega=2 \pi \times 330 \\ & 2 \pi f=2 \pi \times 330 \\ & f=330\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A sinusoidal wave of wavelength 7.5 cm travels a distance of 1.2 cm along the x -direction in 0.3 sec. The crest $P$ is at $x=0$ at $t=0 \mathrm{sec}$ and maximum displacement of the wave is 2 cm. Which equation correctly represents this wave ?
questions.explanation:
$\begin{aligned}

& \mathrm{v}=\frac{\text { distance }}{\text { time }} \\ & \mathrm{v}=\frac{12}{0.3}=4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{k}=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}=\frac{2 \pi}{7.5}=\frac{4 \pi}{15}=0.83 \\ & \mathrm{v}=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{k}} \Rightarrow \omega=\mathrm{vk}=4 \times \frac{4 \pi}{15}=3.35

\end{aligned}$

So $y=A \cos (k x-\omega t)$

questions.question: A sound wave of frequency $245\mathrm{Hz}$ travels with the speed of $300{ms}^{ - 1}$ along the positive x-axis. Each point of the wave moves to and fro through a total distance of $6\mathrm{cm}$. What will be the mathematical expression of this travelling wave?
questions.explanation: $\omega = 2\pi f = 1.5 \times {10}^{3} A = \frac{6}{2} = 3\mathrm{cm} = 0.03m$

questions.question: A travelling harmonic wave is represented by the equation $y\left(x,t\right) = {10}^{ - 3}\sin \left(50t + 2x\right)\text{,}$ where $x$ and $y$ are in meter and $t$ is in seconds. Which of the following is a correct statement about the wave?
options: The wave is propagating along the positive $x$ -axis with speed $25m{s}^{ - 1}$
The wave is propagating along the positive $x$ -axis with speed $100m{s}^{ - 1}$
The wave is propagating along the negative $x$ -axis with speed $25m{s}^{ - 1}$
The wave is propagating along the negative $x$ -axis with speed $100m{s}^{ - 1}$
questions.explanation:
Given wave equation, $y\left(x,t\right) = {10}^{ - 3}\sin \left(50t + 2x\right)$

This equation is similar to the equation of wave travelling along the negative $x$-axis which is given by

$y\left(x,t\right) = A\sin \left(\omega t + kx\right)$

After comparing, Angular frequency $\omega = 50{s}^{ - 1}$

Wave number $k = 2{m}^{ - 1}$

The wave velocity, $v = \frac{\omega }{k} = \frac{50}{2} = 25m{s}^{ - 1}$

`

questions.question: A point source is emitting sound waves of intensity $16 \times {10}^{ - 8}W{m}^{ - 2}$ at the origin. The difference in intensity (magnitude only) at two points located at a distances of $2m$ and $4m$ from the origin respectively will be ________$\times {10}^{ - 8}W{m}^{ - 2}$.
questions.explanation:
Intensity for a point source varies as $I \propto \frac{1}{{r}^{2}}$.

Intensity at a distance of $2m$, {I}_{2} = 16 \times {10}^{ - 8} \times \frac{1}{{2}^{2}} = 4 \times {10}^{ - 8}W{m}^{ - 2}$

Similarly, intensity at a distance of $4m$, {I}_{4} = 16 \times {10}^{ - 8} \times \frac{1}{{4}^{2}} = 1 \times {10}^{ - 8}W{m}^{ - 2}$

Required difference, {I}_{2} - {I}_{4} = 3 \times {10}^{ - 8}W{m}^{ - 2}$

questions.question: Two travelling waves of equal amplitudes and equal frequencies move in opposite directions along a string. They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by $y = \left(10\cos \pi x\sin \frac{2\pi t}{T}\right)\mathrm{cm}$. The amplitude of the particle at $x = \frac{4}{3}\mathrm{cm}$ will be _____ $\mathrm{cm}.$
questions.explanation:
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position, for that

$\sin \left(\frac{2\pi t}{T}\right) = 1$

Therefore, $A = \left(10\cos \left(\frac{4}{3}\pi \right)\right) = 10 \times \frac{1}{2} = 5\mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: Two travelling waves produces a standing wave represented by equation. $y = \left(1.0\mathrm{mm}\right)\cos \left(\left(1.57{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 1}\right)x\right)\sin \left(\left(78.5{s}^{ - 1}\right)t\right)$. The node closest to the origin in the region $x > 0$ will be at $x = ......\left(\text{in}\mathrm{cm}\right).$
questions.explanation:
At Node,

$y = 0 \implies \cos \left(1.57x\right)\sin \left(78.5t\right) = 0 \implies \cos (1.57x) = 0 \implies 1.57x = \frac{\pi }{2} \implies x = 1\mathrm{cm}$

questions.question:
The equations of two waves are given by :

{y}_{1} = 5\sin 2\pi \left(x - vt\right)\mathrm{cm} {y}_{2} = 3\sin 2\pi \left(x - vt + 1.5\right)\mathrm{cm}$

These waves are simultaneously passing through a string. The amplitude of the resulting wave is :
questions.explanation:
Given equations can be written as,

{y}_{1} = 5\sin \left(2\pi x - 2\pi vt\right)\mathrm{cm}$ and

{y}_{2} = 3\sin \left(2\pi x - 2\pi vt + 3\pi \right)\mathrm{cm}$

From the given equations we can conclude that the phase difference between the waves is $3\pi$ i.e. odd multiple of $\pi$. Therefore, destructive interference will happen.

$A = \left({A}_{1} - {A}_{2}\right) = 2\mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: Two light beams of intensities in the ratio of $9 : 4$ are allowed to interfere. The ratio of the intensity of maxima and minima will be :
questions.explanation:
Data provided in the question is, the ratio of the intensities,

$\frac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} = \frac{9}{4}$

After taking square root of above equation on both sides, we get,

$\frac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{2}}} = \frac{3}{2}$

Apply componendo and dividendo,

$\implies \frac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}} = \frac{3 + 2}{3 - 2} = \frac{5}{1} \implies {\left(\frac{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}}\right)}^{2} = \frac{{I}_{\max }}{{I}_{\min }} = \frac{25}{1}$

,

questions.question: If a wave gets refracted into a denser medium, then which of the following is true?
options: Wavelength increases, speed decreases and frequency remains constant.
Wavelength and speed decreases but frequency remains constant.
questions.explanation:
In refraction from one medium to another, the speed and wavelength gets changed. The frequency remains unchanged.

questions.question: Two light beams of intensities $4I$ and $9I$ interfere on a screen. The phase difference between these beams on the screen at point $A$ is zero and at point $B$ is $\pi$. The difference of resultant intensities, at the point $A$ and $B$, will be _____ $I$.
questions.explanation:
The resultant intensity is given by {I}_{\mathrm{net}} = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} + 2\sqrt{{I}_{1}}\sqrt{{I}_{2}}\cos ϕ$

Now, for {I}_{\max }$, phase angle is $ϕ = 0$ and for {I}_{\min }$, phase angle is $ϕ = \pi$.

Thus, {I}_{\max } = {\left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} + \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\sqrt{9I} + \sqrt{4I}\right)}^{2} = 25I$

And {I}_{\min } = {\left(\sqrt{{I}_{1}} - \sqrt{{I}_{2}}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\sqrt{9I} - \sqrt{4I}\right)}^{2} = I$

The difference of resultant intensities is {I}_{\max } - {I}_{\min } = 25I - I = 24I$

questions.question: Three harmonic waves having equal frequency $v$ and same intensity {I}_{0}$ , have phase angles $0,\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $- \frac{\pi }{4}$ respectively. When they are superimposed the intensity of the resultant wave is close to:
questions.explanation: {A}_{R} = \left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)A {I}_{R} = {\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}{I}_{0} = \left(3 + 2\sqrt{2}\right){I}_{0} = 5.8{I}_{0}$

questions.question: The displacement equations of two interfering waves are given by {y}_{1} = 10\sin \left(\omega t + \frac{\pi }{3}\right)\mathrm{cm}$, {y}_{2} = 5\left(\sin \left(\omega t\right) + \sqrt{3}\cos \omega t\right)\mathrm{cm}$ respectively. The amplitude of the resultant wave is _____ $\mathrm{cm}$.
questions.explanation:
Displacement equation of second wave can be written as,{y}_{2} = 5\left(\sin \omega t + \sqrt{3}\cos \omega t\right)\; = 10\sin \left(\omega t + \frac{\pi }{3}\right)$

As we can see, the phase difference between the waves is $0$. Therefore, resultant amplitude will be sum of the amplitudes of the waves.

So $A = {A}_{1} + {A}_{2} = 10\mathrm{cm} + 10\mathrm{cm} = 20\mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: Two waves are simultaneously passing through a string and their equations are : {y}_{1} = {A}_{1}\sin k(x - vt),{y}_{2} = {A}_{2}\sin k\left(x - vt + {x}_{0}\right).$ Given amplitudes {A}_{1} = 12\mathrm{mm}$ and {A}_{2} = 5\mathrm{mm}$, {x}_{0} = 3.5\mathrm{cm}$ and wave number $k = 6.28{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 1}.$ The amplitude of resulting wave will be _____ $\mathrm{mm}.$
questions.explanation: $\Delta ϕ = {\mathrm{kx}}_{0} = \frac{2\pi }{\lambda }{x}_{0} = 2\pi \times 3.5\left(\lambda = \frac{2\pi }{k} = 1\right) = 2\pi \times \frac{35}{10} = 7\pi {A}_{R} = \sqrt{{12}^{2} + {5}^{2} + 2 \times 12 \times 5 \times \cos (7\pi )} = \sqrt{(12 - 5{)}^{2}} = 7\mathrm{mm}$

questions.question:
A string is clamped at both the ends and it is vibrating in its {4}^{th}$ harmonic. The equation of the stationary wave is $y = 0.3\sin ⁡\left(0.157x\right)cos(200\pi t)$. The length of the string is

(All quantities are in $SI$ units.)
questions.explanation:
From the equation, $k = 0.157 \frac{2\pi }{\lambda } = 0.157 \lambda = 40m$

But, length of the wire in {4}^{\mathrm{th}}$ harmonic, $l = 4 \times \frac{\lambda }{2} = 2\lambda = 80m$.

questions.question: A student is performing the experiment of the resonance column. The diameter of the column tube is $6\mathrm{cm}$. The frequency of the tuning fork is $504\mathrm{Hz}$. Speed of the sound at the given temperature is $336m{s}^{ - 1}$. The zero of the meter scale coincides with the top end of the resonance column tube. The reading of the water level in the column when the first resonance occurs is:
questions.explanation: $d = 6\mathrm{cm},f = 504,v = 336m{s}^{ - 1} e = 0.3d l + e = \frac{\lambda }{4} = \frac{V}{4f} l = 16.66 - 0.3 \times 6 l = 14.866\mathrm{cm} l = 14.8\mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: In an experiment with a closed organ pipe, it is filled with water by $\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)$ th of its volume. The frequency of the fundamental note will change by
questions.explanation: $\lambda_1=4 \ell \mathrm{f}_1=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}$ $\begin{aligned} & \lambda_2=\frac{16 \ell}{5} \\ & \mathrm{f}_2=\frac{5 \mathrm{~V}}{16 \ell} \\ & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\ell}\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)}{\frac{\mathrm{V}}{4 \ell}} \times 100=25 \%\end{aligned}$ ;

questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is equal to the first overtone frequency of an open organ pipe. If length of the open pipe is $60\mathrm{cm}$, the length of the closed pipe will be :
questions.explanation: $\frac{\lambda }{4} = {L}_{1}2\left(\frac{\lambda }{2}\right) = {L}_{2} \text{As},v = f\lambda \implies {f}_{2} = \frac{2v}{2{L}_{2}} \implies v = {f}_{1}\left(4{L}_{1}\right) \implies {f}_{2} = \frac{v}{{L}_{2}} \implies {f}_{1} = \frac{v}{4{L}_{1}}$ As per question, {f}_{1} = {f}_{2} \frac{v}{4{L}_{1}} = \frac{v}{{L}_{2}} \implies {L}_{2} = 4{L}_{1} \implies 60 = 4 \times {L}_{1} \implies {L}_{1} = 15\mathrm{cm}$ !

questions.question: A one metre long (both ends open) organ pipe is kept in a gas that has double the density of air at STP. Assuming the speed of sound in air at STP is $300m / s,$ the frequency difference between the fundamental and second harmonic of this pipe is __________ Hz.
questions.explanation: $V = \sqrt{\frac{B}{\rho }} \frac{{V}_{pipe}}{{V}_{air}} = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{B}{2\rho }}}{\sqrt{\frac{B}{\rho }}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} {V}_{pipe} = \frac{{V}_{air}}{\sqrt{2}} {f}_{n} = \frac{(n + 1){V}_{pipe}}{2l} {f}_{1} - {f}_{0} = \frac{{V}_{pipe}}{2l} = \frac{300}{2\sqrt{2}} = 105.75Hz\left(if\sqrt{2} = 1.41\right) = 106.05Hz\left(if\sqrt{2} = 1.414\right)$

questions.question: In a resonance tube experiment when the tube is filled with water up to a height of $17.0\mathrm{cm}\text{,}$ from bottom, it resonates with a given tuning fork. When the water level is raised the next resonance with the same tuning fork occurs at a height of $24.5\mathrm{cm}\text{.}$ If the velocity of sound in air is $330m{s}^{ - 1}\text{,}$ the tuning fork frequency is :
questions.explanation: $\frac{\lambda }{2} = 24.5 - 17 = 7.5\mathrm{cm} f = \frac{V}{\lambda } = \frac{330 \times 100}{15} = 2200\mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: A closed organ pipe has a fundamental frequency of $1.5\text{ }\mathrm{kHz}$. The number of overtones that can be distinctly heard by a person with this organ pipe will be $($Assume that the highest frequency a person can hear is $20,000\text{ }\mathrm{Hz}$).
questions.explanation:
For a closed organ pipe, the resonate frequency(harmonics) is an odd multiple of the fundamental frequency.

Therefore, $\left(2n - 1\right){f}_{0} \le 20000\mathrm{Hz}$, where $n = 1,2,3... {f}_{0} = 1.5\mathrm{kHz} \implies$ fundamental frequency

Then, $n = 7$

The total number of overtones that can be heard is $6$. ({2}^{\mathrm{nd}}$ harmonic to {7}^{\mathrm{th}}$ harmonic. )

.

questions.question: In the resonance experiment, two air columns (closed at one end) of 100 cm and 120 cm long, give 15 beats per second when each one is sounding in the respective fundamental modes. The velocity of sound in the air column is :
questions.explanation:
Fundamental frequency in close/organ pipe

$\begin{aligned} & (\mathrm{f})=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell} \\ & \mathrm{f}_1=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell_1} \& \mathrm{f}_2=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell_2}\end{aligned}$

Beat $=\left(\mathrm{f}_1-\mathrm{f}_2\right)=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4}\left(\frac{1}{\ell_1}-\frac{1}{\ell_2}\right) \begin{aligned} & 15=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4}\left(\frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{1.2}\right) \\ & \mathrm{v}=\left(\frac{15 \times 4 \times 1.2}{0.2}\right)=60 \times 6=360 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$ ,

questions.question: A closed organ and an open organ tube are filled by two different gases having same bulk modulus but different densities $\rho_1$ and $\rho_{2^{\prime}}$, respectively. The frequency of $9^{\text {th }}$ harmonic of closed tube is identical with $4^{\text {th }}$ harmonic of open tube. If the length of the closed tube is 10 cm and the density ratio of the gases is $\rho_1: \rho_2=1: 16$, then the length of the open tube is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & 9^{\text {th }} \text { harmonic of closed pipe }=\frac{9 \mathrm{~V}_1}{4 \ell_1} \\ & 4^{\text {th }} \text { harmonic of open pipe }=\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\ell_2} \\ & \therefore \frac{9 \mathrm{~V}_1}{4 \ell_1}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}_2}{\ell_2} \\ & \therefore \frac{9}{4 \ell_1} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{~B}}{\rho_1}}=\frac{2}{\ell_2} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{~B}}{\rho_2}} \Rightarrow \frac{\ell_2}{\ell_1}=\frac{8}{9} \sqrt{\frac{\rho_1}{\rho_2}} \\ & \ell_2=\ell_1 \times \frac{8}{9} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{20}{9} \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$ ;

questions.question: An organ pipe $40\mathrm{cm}$ long is open at both ends. The speed of sound in air is $360m{s}^{ - 1}$. The frequency of the second harmonic is _$________\mathrm{Hz}.$
questions.explanation:
The formula for the frequency in an open organ pipe is

$f = \frac{nv}{2L}$

Since, it is a second harmonic, $n = 2$

The frequency of the second harmonic becomes $f = \frac{2v}{2L} = \frac{v}{L}$

The data given is

$L = 0.4m\;$

Substituting the values in the frequency formula

$f = \frac{360m{s}^{ - 1}}{0.4m} = 900\mathrm{Hz}$

questions.question: Two open organ pipes of lengths $60 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ resonate at $6^{\text {th }}$ and $5^{\text {th }}$ harmonics respectively. The difference of frequencies for the given modes is _______ $\mathrm{Hz}$. (Velocity of sound in air $=333 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.explanation: The difference in frequency in open organ pipe $= \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}=\frac{\mathrm{nv}}{2 \mathrm{~L}} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{f}=\frac{6 \mathrm{v}}{2 \times 0.6}-\frac{5 \mathrm{v}}{2 \times 0.9} \\ & \mathrm{v}=333 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{f}=740 \mathrm{~Hz} \end{aligned}$

questions.question: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of $20.0\mathrm{cm}$ for a tuning fork of frequency $400\mathrm{Hz}$ is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is $336{ms}^{ - 1}$. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____ $\mathrm{cm}$
questions.explanation:
Wavelength of wave $\implies \lambda = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{336}{400} = 84\mathrm{cm}$

At first resonance

$\frac{\lambda }{4} = l + e \implies \frac{84}{4} = 20 + e$, where, $e$ is end correction.

$\implies e = 1$

So third resonance length

$5\frac{\lambda }{4} = {l}_{2} + e 5\left(21\right) = {l}_{2} + 1 {l}_{2} = 104\mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: A closed and an open organ pipe have same lengths. If the ratio of frequencies of their seventh overtones is $\left(\frac{a-1}{a}\right)$ then the value of $\mathrm{a}$ is ________
questions.explanation: For closed organ pipe $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}=(2 \mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}=\frac{15 \mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}$ For open organ pipe $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=(\mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \ell}=\frac{8 \mathrm{v}}{2 \ell} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}}=\frac{15}{16}=\frac{\mathrm{a}-1}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=16\end{aligned}$ ,

questions.question: In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of fundamental note is $30\mathrm{Hz}$. A certain amount of water is now poured in the organ pipe so that the fundamental frequency is increased to $110\mathrm{Hz}$. If the organ pipe has a cross-sectional area of $2{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}$, the amount of water poured in the organ tube is ________$g$. (Take speed of sound in air is $330m{s}^{ - 1}$ )
questions.explanation:
Fundamental frequency for closed organ pipe in the first part:

$\frac{V}{4{l}_{1}} = 30 \implies {l}_{1} = \frac{11}{4}m$

Similarly, for second part:

$\frac{V}{4{l}_{2}} = 110 \implies {l}_{2} = \frac{3}{4}m$

Therefore, change in length $\Delta l = 2m$

Change in volume $= \mathrm{AΔ}l = 400{\mathrm{cm}}^{3} M = 400g;\left(∵\rho = 1g{\mathrm{cm}}^{ - 3}\right)$

,

questions.question: For a certain organ pipe, the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of $1 : 3 : 5$ respectively. If the frequency of fifth harmonic is $405\mathrm{Hz}$ and the speed of sound in air is $324m{s}^{–1}$ the length of the organ pipe is _____ $m$.
questions.explanation:
It is given,

{f}_{5} = 405\mathrm{Hz}$.

As the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of $1 : 3 : 5$, therefore it must be a closed organ pipe.

The frequency formula in a closed organ pipe is given by $f = \frac{nv}{4l}$. So,

$\frac{5v}{4I} = 405\mathrm{Hz} \implies I = \frac{405 \times 4}{5 \times 324} = 1m$

!

questions.question: A tuning fork is vibrating at $250\mathrm{Hz}$. The length of the shortest closed organ pipe that will resonate with the tuning fork will be _____$\mathrm{cm}$. (Take speed of sound in air as $340{ms}^{ - 1}$ )
questions.explanation:
For closed organ pipe

$f = (2n + 1)\frac{v}{4l}$

for minimum length, $n = 0 {f}_{0} = \frac{v}{4l} \implies l = \frac{v}{4{f}_{0}} = \frac{340}{4 \times 250} = 34\mathrm{cm}$

`

questions.question: The ratio of speed of sound in hydrogen gas to the speed of sound in oxygen gas at the same temperature is:
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the speed of sound in hydrogen gas is given by

{v}_{{H}_{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{{M}_{{H}_{2}}}}...\left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the speed of sound in oxygen is given by

{v}_{{O}_{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{{M}_{{O}_{2}}}}...\left(2\right)$

Divide equation (1) by (2) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

$\frac{{v}_{{H}_{2}}}{{v}_{{O}_{2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{{M}_{{O}_{2}}}{{M}_{{H}_{2}}}}...\left(3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

$\begin{matrix}\frac{{v}_{{H}_{2}}}{{v}_{{O}_{2}}} & = & \sqrt{\frac{32}{2}} \\ & = & 4 : 1\end{matrix}$

questions.question: For a solid rod, the Young's modulus of elasticity is $3.2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{ - 2}$ and density is $8 \times {10}^{3}\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$. The velocity of longitudinal wave in the rod will be
questions.explanation:
The velocity of longitudinal wave in the rod will be, $v = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho }}\; = 2 \times {10}^{3}\sqrt{10} \approx 6.32 \times {10}^{3}m{s}^{ - 1}$

:

questions.question: A person standing on an open ground hears the sound of a jet aeroplane, coming from north at an angle {60}^{o}$ with ground level, but he finds the aeroplane right vertically above his position. If $v$ is the speed of sound, speed of the plane is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{d}{{v}_{s}} = \frac{d\text{ }cos{60}^{o}}{{v}_{a}} {v}_{a} = \frac{{v}_{s}}{2} = \frac{v}{2}$ ;

questions.question:
The speed of sound in oxygen at S.T.P. will be approximately:

(Given, $R = 8.3J{K}^{ - 1},\gamma = 1.4)$
questions.explanation:
The speed of sound is given by,

$v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{M}}\; = 314.8541≃315m{s}^{ - 1}$

Nearest answer given in the option is $310m{s}^{ - 1}$.

questions.question: Two strings with circular cross section and made of same material, are stretched to have same amount of tension. A transverse wave is then made to pass through both the strings. The velocity of the wave in the first string having the radius of cross section R is $\mathrm{v}_1$, and that in the other string having radius of cross section $R / 2$ is $v_2$. Then $\frac{v_2}{v_1}=$
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}=\sqrt{\frac{T}{f \pi R^2}} \\ & \frac{v_2}{v_1}=\frac{R_1}{R_2}=2\end{aligned}$

questions.question: Sound travels in a mixture of two moles of helium and $n$ moles of hydrogen. If rms speed of gas molecules in the mixture is $\sqrt{2}$ times the speed of sound, then the value of $n$ will be
questions.explanation:
Speed of sound in a gas is given by, {v}_{s} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{M}}$

The formula for RMS speed is, {v}_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$

It is given that {v}_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{2}{v}_{s} \implies \frac{{v}_{s}}{{v}_{\mathrm{rms}}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma }{3}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies \frac{\gamma }{3} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \gamma = \frac{3}{2}$

For $\gamma$ of mixture,

{\gamma }_{\mathrm{mix}} = \frac{{C}_{P,mix}}{{C}_{V,mix}} = \frac{\frac{2{C}_{P,H} + n{C}_{P,He}}{2 + n}}{\frac{2{C}_{V,H} + n{C}_{V,He}}{2 + n}}$

Since Hydrogen is a diatomic gas, {C}_{V,H} = \frac{5}{2}R,{C}_{P,H} = \frac{7}{2}R$ and Helium is monatomic gas, {C}_{V,He} = \frac{3}{2}R,{C}_{P,He} = \frac{5}{2}R$. Therefore,

{\gamma }_{\mathrm{mix}} = \frac{\frac{2{C}_{P,H} + n{C}_{P,He}}{2 + n}}{\frac{2{C}_{V,H} + n{C}_{V,He}}{2 + n}}\; \implies n = 2$

!

questions.question: The fundamental frequency of vibration of a string between two rigid support is $50\mathrm{Hz}$. The mass of the string is $18g$ and its linear mass density is $20g{m}^{ - 1}$. The speed of the transverse waves so produced in the string is _______ $m{s}^{–1}$.
questions.explanation:
The fundamental frequency is $f = 50\mathrm{Hz}$.

The length of the string is $l = \frac{\lambda }{2}$

Linear mass density is $\mu = \frac{m}{l} = 20g{m}^{ - 1}$

Using $v = f\lambda \frac{v}{2l} = 50 \implies v = 100 \times l = \frac{100 \times 18}{20} = 90m{s}^{ - 1}$

questions.question: The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive $x$-direction is given by $y = \frac{1}{(1 + x{)}^{2}}$ at time $t = 0$ and $y = \frac{1}{1 + (x - 2{)}^{2}}$ at $t = 1s$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be $m{s}^{ - 1}.$
questions.explanation:
At $t = 0,y = \frac{1}{1 + {x}^{2}}$

At time $t = t,y = \frac{1}{1 + (x - vt{)}^{2}}$

At $t = 1,y = \frac{1}{1 + (x - v{)}^{2}} \dots (i)$

At $t = 1,y = \frac{1}{1 + (x - 2{)}^{2}} \dots (\mathrm{ii})$

Comparing $(i)\mathrm{and}(\mathrm{ii}) v = 2m{s}^{ - 1}$ .

questions.question: The speed of a transverse wave passing through a string of length $50\mathrm{cm}$ and mass $10g$ is $60m{s}^{ - 1}$. The area of cross-section of the wire is $2.0{\mathrm{mm}}^{2}$ and its Young's modulus is $1.2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{ - 2}$. The extension of the wire over its natural length due to its tension will be $x \times {10}^{ - 5}m$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.explanation:
The wave speed in string is given by {v}_{w} = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }}$, where, $T$ is tension and $\mu = \frac{m}{l}$ is linear mass density.

Putting the values, we have

$\implies 60 = \sqrt{\frac{T}{10 \times {10}^{ - 3}} \times 0.5} \implies T = \frac{{\left(60\right)}^{2} \times {10}^{ - 2}}{0.5} = 72N$

The Young's modulus is given by $Y = \frac{Fl}{A \Delta l}$, here, $A$ is area.

From above the extension of the wire is $\Delta l = \frac{Tl}{AY} = \frac{72 \times 0.5}{2 \times {10}^{ - 6} \times 1.2 \times {10}^{11}} = \frac{72 \times 5}{24} \times {10}^{ - 5} = 15 \times {10}^{ - 5}m$.

Hence, the value of $x = 15$.

:

questions.question: Two identical strings $X$ and $Z$ made of same material have tension {T}_{X}$ and {T}_{Z}$ in then if their fundamental frequencies are $450\mathrm{Hz}$ and $300\mathrm{Hz}$, respectively, then the ratio {T}_{X} / {T}_{Z}$ is :
questions.explanation: $\begin{matrix}{f}_{X} = \frac{1}{2ℓ}\sqrt{\frac{{T}_{X}}{\mu }}\end{matrix} \begin{matrix}{f}_{Z} = \frac{1}{2ℓ}\sqrt{\frac{{T}_{Z}}{\mu }}\end{matrix} \begin{matrix}\frac{{f}_{X}}{{f}_{Z}} = \frac{450}{300} = \sqrt{\frac{{T}_{X}}{{T}_{Z}}} \\ \end{matrix} \implies {T}_{X} / {T}_{Z} = 9 / 4 = 2.25$

questions.question: A wire of length $L$ and mass per unit length $6.0 \times {10}^{ - 3}kg{m}^{ - 1}$ is put under tension of $540N.$ Two consecutive frequencies that it resonates at are: $420Hz$ and $490Hz.$ Then $L$ in meters is :
questions.explanation: Fundamental frequency $= 490 - 420 = 70Hz 70 = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }} \implies 70 = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{540}{6 \times {10}^{ - 3}}} \implies L = \frac{1}{2 \times 70}\sqrt{90 \times {10}^{3}} = \frac{300}{140} \implies L \approx 2.14m$ ,

questions.question: A sonometer wire of resonating length $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ has a fundamental frequency of $400 \mathrm{~Hz}$ when kept under some tension. The resonating length of the wire with fundamental frequency of $600 \mathrm{~Hz}$ under same tension _____$\mathrm{cm}$.
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_0=400 \mathrm{~Hz} ; \mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mu}}=\text { constant } \\ & \frac{\lambda}{2}=\mathrm{L} ; \quad \mathrm{v}=\mathrm{f}_0 \lambda\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrm{f}_0}=\mathrm{L} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=2 \mathrm{Lf}_0 \\ & \mathrm{~L}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{Lf}_0}{2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{Lf}_0}{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=\frac{90 \times 400}{600}=60\end{aligned}$

questions.question: A wire of length $2L,$ is made by joining two wires $A$ and $B$ of same length but different radii $r$ and $2r$ and made of the same material. It is vibrating at a frequency such that the joint of the two wires forms a node. If the number of antinodes in wire $A$ is $p$ and that in $B$ is $q$ then ratio $p : q$ is:
questions.explanation:
For rod A, {f}_{1} = \frac{{n}_{1}}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\rho {A}_{1}}}$

For rod B, {f}_{2} = \frac{{n}_{2}}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\rho {A}_{2}}}$

Given {f}_{1} = {f}_{2} \frac{{n}_{1}}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\rho {A}_{1}}} = \frac{{n}_{2}}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\rho {A}_{2}}} \frac{{n}_{1}}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\rho {A}_{1}}} = \frac{{n}_{2}}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\rho (4{A}_{1})}}\left(∵ \begin{matrix}{r}_{B} = 2{r}_{A} \\ {A}_{2} = 4{A}_{1}\end{matrix} \right) {n}_{1} = \frac{{n}_{2}}{2} \frac{{n}_{1}}{{n}_{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$

questions.question: A string $2.0m$ long and fixed at its ends is driven by a $240Hz$ vibrator. The string vibrates in its third harmonic mode. The speed of the wave and its fundamental frequency is
questions.explanation:
For a string fixed at both the ends,

$f = \frac{n}{2L}v$

For third harmonic, $240 = \frac{3}{2(2)}v \implies v = \frac{240 \times 4}{3} = 320\text{ }m{s}^{ - 1}$

Fundamental frequency {f}_{0} = \frac{1}{2L}v = \frac{1}{4} \times 320\text{ } = \text{ }80\text{ }Hz$ ;

questions.question: A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length $1m$ stretched with a tension of $6N.$ When the tension in the wire is changed to $54N,$ the same tuning fork produces $12$ beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is _______ $\mathrm{Hz}.$
questions.explanation:
Frequency of sonometer wire is given by, $f = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }}$

Therefore, {f}_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{6}{\mu }} {f}_{2} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{54}{\mu }}$

Hence, $\frac{{f}_{1}}{{f}_{2}} = \frac{1}{3}$

Also it is given that, {f}_{2} - {f}_{1} = 12$

So, {f}_{1} = 6\mathrm{Hz}$.

questions.question: A wire having a linear mass density $9.0 \times {10}^{ - 4}\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 1}$ is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of $900N.$ The wire resonates at a frequency of $500\mathrm{Hz}.$ The next higher frequency at which the same wire resonates is $550\mathrm{Hz}.$ The length of the wire is ___________ $m.$
questions.explanation:
{f}_{n} = \frac{nv}{2ℓ} = 500 {f}_{n + 1} = \frac{(n + 1)v}{2ℓ} = 550 \frac{n + 1}{n} = \frac{11}{10}$

Thus, $n = 10$

Thus, $ℓ = \frac{\mathrm{nv}}{2{f}_{n}}\left(v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }}\right) = \frac{10}{2 \times 500} \times \sqrt{\frac{900}{9 \times {10}^{ - 4}}} = 10m$

questions.question: A wire of length $30\mathrm{cm}$, stretched between rigid supports, has it's {n}^{\mathrm{th}}$ and {\left(n + 1\right)}^{\mathrm{th}}$ harmonics at $400\mathrm{Hz}$ and $450\mathrm{Hz}$, respectively. If tension in the string is $2700N$, it's linear mass density is _____ $\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 1}$.
questions.explanation:
Frequency of {n}^{th}$ harmonic is $\frac{nv}{2l} = 400 \implies \frac{nv}{0.6} = 400...\left(1\right)$

And frequency of {\left(n + 1\right)}^{th}$ harmonic is $\frac{\left(n + 1\right)v}{2l} = 450 \implies \frac{\left(n + 1\right)v}{0.6} = 450...\left(2\right)$, here, $v$ is speed of wave on string.

From equation $\left(1\right)$, we have

$n = \frac{400 \times 0.6}{v}$

Putting in equation $\left(2\right)$,

$\implies \left(\frac{0.6 \times 400}{v} + 1\right)\frac{v}{0.6} = 450 \implies \left(400 + \frac{v}{0.6}\right) = 450 \implies v = 30m{s}^{ - 1}$

Speed of wave on string is stated as $v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }} = 30$, here, $\mu$ is linear mass density.

So, $\mu = \frac{T}{{v}^{2}} = \frac{2700}{900} \implies \mu = 3\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 1}$

;

questions.question: A guitar string of length $90\mathrm{cm}$ vibrates with a fundamental frequency of $120\mathrm{Hz}$. The length of the string producing a fundamental of $180\mathrm{Hz}$ will be _____ $\mathrm{cm}$
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency produced in a vibrating string is given by

{f}_{0} = \frac{v}{2L}...\left(1\right)$

For the first case, it can be written that

$120 = \frac{v}{2(90)}...\left(2\right)$

Similarly, for the second case, it can be written that

$180 = \frac{v}{2(L)}...\left(3\right)$

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) and solve to obtain the required length of the string.

$\begin{matrix}\frac{180}{120} & = & \frac{\frac{v}{2\left(L\right)}}{\frac{v}{2\left(90\right)}} \\ & = & \frac{90}{L} \\ & \implies & L = 90 \times \frac{120}{180} \\ & = & 60\end{matrix}$

`

questions.question: In an experiment with sonometer when a mass of $180g$ is attached to the string, it vibrates with fundamental frequency of $30\mathrm{Hz}$. When a mass $m$ is attached, the string vibrates with fundamental frequency of $50\mathrm{Hz}$. The value of $m$ is ______ $g$.
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency in a stretched string is given by

$f = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }}...\left(1\right)$

For the first mass, it can be written that

{f}_{1} = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{{m}_{1}g}{\mu }}...\left(2\right)$

And, for the second mass, it can be written that

{f}_{2} = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{{m}_{2}g}{\mu }}...\left(3\right)$

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required mass.

$\begin{matrix}\frac{{f}_{2}}{{f}_{1}} & = & \frac{\frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{{m}_{2}g}{\mu }}}{\frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{{m}_{1}g}{\mu }}} \\ & = & \sqrt{\frac{{m}_{2}}{{m}_{1}}} \\ & \implies & \frac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = {\left(\frac{{f}_{1}}{{f}_{2}}\right)}^{2} \\ & \implies & {m}_{2} = {m}_{1}{\left(\frac{{f}_{2}}{{f}_{1}}\right)}^{2}...\left(4\right)\end{matrix}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (4) to calculate the required mass.

$\begin{matrix}{m}_{2} & = & 180g \times {\left(\frac{50}{}\right)}^{2} \\ & = & 500g\end{matrix}$

!

questions.question: A wire of density $8 \times {10}^{3}\mathrm{kg}{m}^{ - 3}$ is stretched between two clamps $0.5m$ apart. The extension developed in the wire is $3.2 \times {10}^{ - 4}m$. If $Y = 8 \times {10}^{10}N{m}^{ - 2}$, the fundamental frequency of vibration in the wire will be _____ $\mathrm{Hz}$
questions.explanation:
Using the relation of Young's modulus,

$\frac{T}{A} = Y\left(\frac{\Delta L}{L}\right) \implies T = \left(\frac{Y\Delta L}{L} \times A\right)$

The linear mass density is $\mu = \left(\frac{m}{L}\right)$.

So,

$\frac{T}{\mu } = \frac{Y\Delta LA}{L\left(\frac{m}{L}\right)} = \frac{Y(\Delta L) \times LA}{L(m)} = \left(\frac{Y\Delta L}{L}\right) \times \left(\frac{1}{\rho }\right)$

Substituting the values,

$\frac{T}{\mu } = \frac{8 \times {10}^{10} \times 3.2 \times {10}^{ - 4}}{0.5} \times \left(\frac{1}{8 \times {10}^{3}}\right) = 6.4 \times {10}^{3} \implies \frac{T}{\mu } = 64 \times {10}^{2}$

The fundamental frequency is given by $f = \frac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }}$.

$\implies \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu }} = 8 \times 10 = 80m{s}^{ - 1}$

Therefore,

$f = \left(\frac{80}{1}\right) = 80\mathrm{Hz}$

;

questions.question: The correct figure that shows, schematically, the wave pattern produced by the superposition of two waves of frequencies $9Hz$ and$11Hz$, is
questions.explanation:
Beat frequency $= 11 - 9 = 2\text{ }Hz$

No.of maxima per second is 2.

Time period of beat $= \frac{1}{2}\text{ }s.$

questions.question: A radar sends an electromagnetic signal of electric field $\left({E}_{0}\right) = 2.25V{m}^{ - 1}$ and magnetic field $\left({B}_{0}\right) = 1.5 \times {10}^{ - 8}T$ which strikes a target on line of sight at a distance of $3\mathrm{km}$ in a medium. After that, a part of signal (echo) reflects back towards the radar with same velocity and by same path. If the signal was transmitted at time $t = 0$ from radar, then after how much time echo will reach to the radar?
questions.explanation:
The speed of light is given by,

$c = \frac{{E}_{0}}{{B}_{0}} = \frac{2.25}{1.5 \times {10}^{ - 8}} = 1.5 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{ - 1}$

Therefore, time taken for the echo will be,

$t = \frac{2d}{c} = \frac{6 \times {10}^{3}}{1.5 \times {10}^{8}} = 4 \times {10}^{ - 5}s$

`

questions.question: The velocity of sound in a gas, in which two wavelengths $4.08m$ and $4.16m$ produce $40$ beats in $12s$, will be
questions.explanation:
If the velocity of the sound in the medium is $v$ then, {f}_{1} = \frac{v}{4.08}$ and {f}_{2} = \frac{v}{4.16}$

Now beat frequency,

{f}_{b} = \Delta f = \left({f}_{1} - {f}_{2}\right) = \frac{40}{12} = \frac{10}{3}\mathrm{Hz}\;$

questions.question: A tuning fork $A$ of unknown frequency produces $5\mathrm{beats}{s}^{ - 1}$ with a fork of known frequency $340\mathrm{Hz}$. When fork $A$ is filed, the beat frequency decreases to $2\mathrm{beats}{s}^{ - 1}$. What is the frequency of fork $A$ ?
questions.explanation:
Initially beat frequency $= 5\mathrm{Hz}$

so, {\rho }_{A} = 340 \pm 5 = 345\mathrm{Hz},$ or $335\mathrm{Hz}$

after filing frequency increases slightly so, new value of frequency of $A > {\rho }_{A}$

Now, beat frequency $= 2\mathrm{Hz} \implies$ new {\rho }_{A} = 340 \pm 2 = 342\mathrm{Hz},$ or $338\mathrm{Hz}$

hence, original frequency of $A$ is {\rho }_{A} = 335\mathrm{Hz}$

,

questions.question: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{a} \cos (1.5 \mathrm{t}) \cos (50.5 \mathrm{t})$ where $t$ is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat (close to nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
The given equation can be written as

$\mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2} \cos [1.5+50.5] \mathrm{t}+\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2} \cos [50.5-1.5] x=\frac{a}{2} \cos [52 t]+\frac{a}{2} \cos [49 t]$

Here, $2 \pi \mathrm{f}_1 \& 2 \pi \mathrm{f}_2=49 \mathrm{f}_1=\frac{52}{2 \pi}, \mathrm{f}_2=\frac{49}{2 \pi} \therefore \mathrm{f}_{\text {Bat }}=\mathrm{f}_1-\mathrm{f}_2=\frac{3}{2 \pi} \mathrm{~Hz} \therefore \mathrm{T}_{\text {Beat }}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\text {Beat }}}=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \mathrm{sec} =2.09 \mathrm{sec} \approx 2 \mathrm{sec}$ !

questions.question: A set of $20$ tuning forks is arranged in a series of increasing frequencies. If each fork gives $4$ beats with respect to the preceding fork and the frequency of the last fork is twice the frequency of the first, then the frequency of last fork is _____ $\mathrm{Hz}$.
questions.explanation: Each fork produces $4$ beats per second with the previous means each fork has frequency $4\mathrm{Hz}$ more than the previous. Using relation, {f}_{\mathrm{last}} = {f}_{\mathrm{first}} + \left(N - 1\right)x$, here, $N$ is the number of tuning fork in series and $x$ is beat frequency between two successive forks. $2{f}_{0} = {f}_{0} + \left(20 - 1\right)4 \implies 2{f}_{0} = {f}_{0} + 76\;$ Frequency of last tuning fork is $152\mathrm{Hz}$.

questions.question: A small speaker delivers $2W$ of audio output. At what distance from the speaker will one detect $120dB$ intensity sound? [Given reference intensity of sound as {10}^{ - 12}W / {m}^{2}$ ]
questions.explanation: Let the intensity of sound hear by observer is $I 120 = 10{\log }_{10}⁡\frac{I}{{10}^{ - 12}} 12 = \log ⁡I - {\log }_{10}⁡{10}^{ - 12} = \log ⁡I + 12 \log ⁡I = 0 \implies I = 1\frac{watt}{{m}^{2}} I = \frac{P}{4\pi {r}^{2}} \implies 1 = \frac{2}{4\pi {r}^{2}} \implies r = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }} = 0.4m = 40cm$
